meta.title: MoonClip — Local-first clip recorder for Linux and Windows
meta.description: MoonClip is a local-first clip recorder for Linux and Windows. A Medal.tv-style alternative with zero cloud: replay buffer, lightweight editor and sharing through your own storage. Open source and 100% local.
hero.tagline: Local-first clip recorder for Linux and Windows
hero.description: A Medal.tv alternative with zero cloud: one-key replay buffer, local gallery and sharing through your own storage (Google Drive) and webhooks. Open source, lightweight and 100% local — no accounts, no telemetry, no foreign cloud.
hero.releases: Downloads are published on the Releases page.

features.title: Features
features.subtitle: Everything you need to capture, keep and share your clips, without depending on a cloud.
features.buffer.title: Replay buffer with F9
features.buffer.text: Replay loop with the integrated gpu-screen-recorder engine (Linux): save the last seconds with one key from the tray, with mixed-first audio.
features.audio.title: Per-track audio
features.audio.text: Three audio tracks (mixed, game and chat) with live gains, Medal-style CBR encoding with NVENC HQ at 30/60 fps.
features.gallery.title: Local gallery
features.gallery.text: Gallery with thumbnails and real durations, no cloud. Your clips live on your disk and are saved with lanczos scaling.
features.privacy.title: Cloud-free data
features.privacy.text: SQLite settings with relative paths, credentials in the OS keyring and monitor selection. Portable: everything next to the app.
features.windows.title: Windows capture
features.windows.text: Windows port with WGC capture and WASAPI audio on AMF/QSV encoders. It is the next development phase.
features.editor.title: Editor and sharing
features.editor.text: Timeline editor (trim, vertical and remix) and publishing to your own storage (Google Drive) and webhooks. Planned for later phases.
inspiration.title: Inspired by Medal.tv's idea
inspiration.text: Medal.tv popularized the idea of saving clips from your matches with a single touch. MoonClip takes that same idea and turns it into a similar open-source program: like Office and LibreOffice, same idea, different philosophy.
inspiration.local.title: 100% local
inspiration.local.text: Your clips live on your disk, not in a cloud.
inspiration.opensource.title: Open source
inspiration.opensource.text: Free software under GPL-3.0, with gpu-screen-recorder as the engine on Linux.
inspiration.nocloud.title: No mandatory accounts
inspiration.nocloud.text: No registration and no telemetry; sharing goes through your own storage.
inspiration.private.title: Private by default
inspiration.private.text: Nothing is shared unless you publish it yourself.
requirements.title: Requirements
requirements.item1: Linux (X11/Wayland): current phase, with gpu-screen-recorder as the capture engine.
requirements.item2: Windows 10/11 x64: on the way (WGC + WASAPI + AMF/QSV).
requirements.item3: A GPU for hardware encoding (NVENC on Linux; QSV/AMF coming soon).

usage.title: Usage
usage.tray.title: Tray + F9
usage.tray.text: The replay buffer is managed from the tray; one key (F9) saves the clip instantly.
usage.gallery.title: Gallery
usage.gallery.text: Thumbnails with real durations, search and delete. All local and instant.
usage.settings.title: Settings
usage.settings.text: Monitor selection, 30/60 fps, encoding quality, per-track gains and keyring credentials.
usage.ui.title: MoonClip interface
usage.ui.text: Frameless UI with its own theme, bilingual (ES/EN).
data.title: Data locations
data.clips.loc: Clips folder, relative to the app data
data.db.loc: SQLite with library, apps and settings
data.portable.loc: Everything next to the app folder
data.note: The app uses relative paths: in portable mode everything lives next to the app folder; when installed, in the OS data directories (e.g. %LOCALAPPDATA% on Windows and ~/.local/share on Linux).
